rules.title: Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions to rent or end a tenancy. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.
citation_aliases: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.effective_date_note: Document states City Council passed the ordinance April 14, 2020; effective date not stated.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages (actual damages or three times one month's rent), punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner lives; units under a rental agreement allowing owner move-back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties where owner resides
units under owner move-back rental agreement
existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

parsed.doc_summary: Berkeley Rent Board page on the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106). It bars criminal-history screening in rental housing and lists exemptions, penalties and complaint procedures. One screening_restrictions rule extracted.
